chunks: Aban narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: A man is owed dinars by another man, so he takes dirhams from him, then the price changes. He said: They belong to him according to the rate at which he took them that day. And if he took dinars, and the other had no dirhams with him, then his dinars remain owed by him, and he may take them in their original amount whenever he wishes.

key_terms.الدَّنَانِيرُ: gold dinars owed as the original debt
key_terms.السِّعْرُ: the exchange rate or market value at the time of payment
key_terms.بِرُءُوسِهَا: in their original principal amount, without increase
key_terms.يَوْمَئِذٍ: that specific day when the exchange or acceptance occurred

ai.seo_question: If a debt owed in dinars is paid in dirhams, which exchange rate should be used?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on settling a debt denominated in one currency with another currency. The ruling is that the settlement is calculated according to the exchange rate on the day of acceptance, while an unpaid debt in dinars remains due in its original principal amount.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4038 - Aban narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)) about a man who is owed dinars by another man, but he accepts dirhams instead. Then the price changes.
Imam (as) said: "It is based on the value at which he accepted them on that day. However, if he had accepted dinars and not dirhams, then his dinars remain owed to him, and he may take them in their original amount whenever he wishes."
